findings.description: The invariant did not bind every marker to its expected logical block.
findings.resolution: Every provider-aware and exact-wait marker is bound to an explicit logical owner with aggregate drift and conflicting-marker checks.
findings.suggestedFix: Retain explicit marker ownership and aggregate inventory checks.

findings.description: The invariant did not originally enforce capability-to-encoding and encoding-to-constructor relationships.
findings.resolution: Exact capability-to-encoding, encoding-to-schema, and encoding-to-constructor relationships are asserted.
findings.suggestedFix: Retain the exact normalized relationship assertions.

findings.description: The original status-read check was not whitespace tolerant.
findings.resolution: Whitespace-normalized checks prove subscription precedes every status read and the receiver reaches the targeted wait.
findings.suggestedFix: Retain normalized ordering and receiver-handoff assertions.

findings.description: The ripgrep URL originally interpolated a project-relative output path.
findings.resolution: Release tag, archive basename, and project-relative destination are separate variables in both publication paths.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep URL basenames separate from local destination paths.

findings.description: Send and follow-up marker checks originally used only aggregate counts.
findings.resolution: Send and follow-up state and delivery blocks are independently bound to exact marker owners.

findings.description: The documented invariant command originally ran from a directory without the applicable justfile.
findings.resolution: Active commands change into the nested workspace before invoking just.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep the required working directory explicit.

findings.description: The release URL originally used the local archive path instead of its basename.
findings.resolution: Both publication paths use an archive basename in the URL and a separate local path.
findings.suggestedFix: Retain separate URL and destination variables.

findings.description: The public tag was originally created from ambient HEAD.
findings.resolution: The public tag is created from and verified against WRAPPER_CANDIDATE_SHA.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep public tag creation explicitly SHA-bound.

findings.description: The release preflight originally validated fetch URLs but not push URLs.
findings.resolution: Every configured fetch and push URL is validated before publication.
findings.suggestedFix: Retain exact fetch- and push-URL checks.

findings.description: The invariant originally omitted five downstream provider-derived encoding hops.
findings.resolution: All handler-to-schema and final communication-constructor hops are asserted.

findings.description: A newly pushed retention tag originally was not resolved and checked before wrapper publication.
findings.resolution: The remote direct or peeled retention tag must equal SUBMODULE_SHA after push.
findings.suggestedFix: Retain post-push exact remote tag verification.

findings.description: Consequential Bash fences originally could continue after failed release operations.
findings.resolution: All consequential Bash fences use fail-fast settings and explicit guards; the only fence without them is a non-mutating process-list example.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep every mutating release fence fail closed.

findings.description: Both verify_release_asset functions are invoked as an if-condition or an AND-list operand, which makes Bash ignore errexit throughout the function. Their unguarded cleanup, directory creation, and gh release download commands can therefore fail and continue; on the persistent manual evidence path, a stale candidate bundle can then satisfy the SHA-256 and four-binary comparisons even when the live release asset was not downloaded, allowing an incorrect digest-less existing asset to be accepted as exact.
findings.resolution: Made both release asset verifiers fail closed and require a fresh regular-file download before digest and binary comparison.
findings.suggestedFix: In both verify_release_asset functions, append `|| return 1` to cleanup, directory creation, and `gh release download`, then require the downloaded path to be a fresh regular file before hashing or extracting it. Keep the existing digest and embedded-binary comparisons.

findings.description: The workflow rejects an existing release unless targetCommitish is the literal GITHUB_SHA. GitHub documents target_commitish as defaulting to the default branch and being unused when the Git tag already exists; releases created by the previous workflow omitted --target. A failed old upload can therefore leave a partial release whose live tag is exactly candidate-bound but whose retry always aborts at this raw metadata comparison instead of repairing the missing asset.
findings.resolution: Used enforced live-tag provenance for existing releases and repaired assets without targetCommitish rejection.
findings.suggestedFix: Use the already-enforced live tag equality as existing-release commit provenance. Do not require raw targetCommitish to equal GITHUB_SHA when the tag exists; retain --target for new releases, then branch on the expected asset's retained digest to skip an exact asset or safely repair only a missing/incorrect one.

findings.sectionRef: Final public-tag and retention-tag publication gate
findings.description: The workflow originally omitted the manual path's final live nested retention-tag equality gate.
findings.resolution: The workflow now resolves direct and peeled release/${RELEASE_VERSION} refs immediately before upload and requires the live SHA to equal SUBMODULE_CANDIDATE_SHA.
findings.suggestedFix: Retain final live retention-tag parity in both publication paths.
